description: A password field with a show/hide button and a Caps Lock warning. For new passwords, a live checklist of your rules. Never renders the value back into the page. Works with Livewire wire:model.

consider.note: Store only a hash: `Hash::make()` or the `hashed` cast, never the password itself, and keep it out of logs, the cache and email. For a new app, consider Argon2id (`HASH_DRIVER=argon2id`, where your PHP has it), OWASP's first choice; bcrypt, Laravel's default, is still fine at cost 12 or more.

With `new`, the checklist only guides typing: a request can send any value. Enforce the same rules with `Password::defaults()` in your Form Request, and consider `->uncompromised()` to turn away passwords already seen in a breach.
Consider throttling sign-in and password reset by email and by IP, so passwords can't be guessed at speed, and answering the same whether or not the account exists.

Hashing is slow on purpose, so check a password once at sign-in and keep the session; don't re-hash on every request. `->uncompromised()` calls an outside API on each submit: keep it to forms that set a new password.
